title: The Last Light
description: An original fictional illustrated mystery, written and directed by the assistant for the owner's requested one-off demonstration. Local synthetic narration and original generated artwork. No Gemini writing, direction or review calls.
hook: The lighthouse had been dark for twelve years. At two thirteen, it started flashing.
payoff: There was no ghost in the lighthouse. Just a dog who refused to leave his person in the dark.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: The lighthouse had been dark for twelve years. At two thirteen, it started flashing.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Across the harbor, Mara put down her tea. Through the rain, the great lantern still looked black.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: But a little ground-floor window blinked three times. Paused. Then four.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Someone would call it a ghost. Mara had a simpler question. Why was the light so low?

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: She took her torch and crossed the causeway. At the cottage door, its beam found muddy pawprints.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: They led inside. From behind the cellar door came a thin bark.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: The old keeper had returned for one last box. He had slipped on the stairs. His phone was upstairs, out of reach.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Beside him waited Pip, the terrier who had followed him everywhere for nine years.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Mara stayed with the keeper until help arrived. But one thing still bothered her. That flashing window.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: While they helped him out, Pip raced back to the sill. There lay an old battery lantern.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: Its loose switch sat beneath a muddy paw. Pip pressed at it. The light flickered, stopped, then flickered again.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: He was not sending a code. He was doing the one thing that had finally made somebody come.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: By dawn, the keeper was safe. Mara knelt beside him, and Pip settled between them.

units.speaker: Narrator
units.text: There was no ghost in the lighthouse. Just a dog who refused to leave his person in the dark.
